The user wants to introduce a guard clause to encapsulate the size check. Currently, `dequeue()`, `getFront()`, and `getRear()` all have the same `if (size == 0) throw new IllegalStateException("Queue is empty")` check, and `enqueue()` has `if (size == capacity) throw new IllegalStateException("Queue is full")`.

I can extract these into private helper methods:
- `requireNonEmpty()` — throws if size == 0
- `requireNonFull()` — throws if size == capacity

This avoids repeating the check inline and gives the guard a meaningful name.
